approved: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would create the Australian Border Force as a single frontline border control and enforcement agency within the Department of Immigration and Border Protection.
It would establish the statutory office of the Australian Border Force Commissioner, who would control operations and also serve as Comptroller-General of Customs.
The bill includes integrity measures such as alcohol and drug screening, secrecy provisions, and serious misconduct management, and would take effect from 1 July 2015.
Establishes the Australian Border Force Commissioner as a statutory officer with operational control of the Australian Border Force.
Allows the Secretary and the Commissioner to issue binding written directions to immigration and border protection workers.
Introduces alcohol and prohibited drug screening tests for immigration and border protection workers.
Provides for resignation and termination of employees involved in serious misconduct.
Immigration and Border Protection workers, including Australian Public Service employees, contractors, consultants, and employees of state, territory and other Commonwealth agencies.

Introduced the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 to create the statutory office of Australian Border Force Commissioner, who will also serve as Comptroller-General of Customs, merging Customs and Immigration into a single front-line agency partly modelled on Operation Sovereign Borders' integrated approach.

Introduced consequential legislation to complete the Australian Border Force integration, citing an Australian Crime Commission estimate that organised crime costs Australia $15 billion annually, extending Law Enforcement Integrity Commissioner oversight to the whole department from 1 July 2015, and allowing resignations to be deferred up to 90 days during misconduct investigations.

Labor supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation, arguing it fulfills a former Labor government commitment to create a single integrated border entity with no greater powers than existing agencies, and includes integrity measures such as drug testing and serious misconduct provisions.

The speaker argued for abolishing the Australian Customs and Border Protection Service and merging its functions with the Department of Immigration and Border Protection to create the Australian Border Force, citing $480.5 million in funding over four years and a track record of no lives lost at sea and over 200 days without boat arrivals.

The speaker supported the Australian Border Force Bill 2015 and related legislation, arguing they establish the Australian Border Force Commissioner and a single integrated border entity with integrity provisions including drug/alcohol testing, serious misconduct declarations, and mandatory reporting, while acknowledging border workers' dedication.
